features: The Florida Candy Factory is an authentic manufacturer of the original 'gourmet' taffy formulation, minus the 'transfat' and 'soy'.

This Eastern Coast recipe, created by a Master Candy Maker, in 1884 at Atlantic City Boardwalk is a bit harder and not mushy compared to other recipes since it has not milk, egg whites or any dairy Product.

To add to the authenticity of the original recipe, our product is cooked in small 270-pound batches to preserve the integrity and quality. In addition, original equipment from the early 1900’s is utilized for cooking, pulling and cutting and wrapping.

description: In 1883 a candy maker on the original Atlantic City Boardwalk was offering his new candy creation called “taffy”. Sales were dismal when an August storm unexpectedly sprayed ocean salt water over his stock. Instead of throwing his “taffy” away, the innovative candy maker changed the name of his creation to “Salt Water” Taffy and sales boomed! Although “ocean salt water” is not an ingredient in our product, a pinch of salt is added to maintain the wonderful title - “Salt Water Taffy. Salt Water Taffy was first cooked in small 10 to 25 pound batches in copper kettles over open fires. The batch was then cooled on marble slab tables and then pulled from a large hook on the wall. Pulling taffy is designed to aerate the candy confection. The candy maker would first hang the batch of cooled taffy from the hook and would then stretch the taffy to 5 or 6 feet from the hook. The puller would then loop the taffy back over the hook, folding itself and trapping air between the two lengths. This aeration process helps to keep the taffy soft. The pulled taffy was then hand rolled on the marble slabs and cut with scissors into approximately ¼” diameter by 2” length pieces. Finally the candy confection was hand wrapped in wax paper with twist ends. Equipment was developed in the early 1900’s to pull, cut & wrap the sweet chewy treats! The Florida Candy Factory, Inc., is an authentic manufacturer of the original “gem of the Atlantic City Boardwalk” salt water taffy formulation, however without the transfat & soy! This “old fashioned” formulation is believed to provide the most desired taste and texture of any of the salt water taffy recipes being manufactured today. To preserve the integrity and quality of the original formulation our taffy is cooked in small batches, utilizing “non high fructose” corn syrup, pure Florida cane sugar, organic palm oil, sunflower lecithin & natural & artificial flavoring.

Baguette

description: Our Handcrafted, All Natural, Wood-Fired Organic Maple Syrup is produced on our Farm, located deep in the Appalachian Valley Great Lake Region of Pennsylvania. It is hand-packed for freshness and exceptional flavor at our farm. Organic Maple Products Vs. Non-Organic We always get the question “What’s not organic about Maple Syrup”? For the most part, I tend to believe that all maple syrup producers make their maple syrup with the upmost integrity. BUT there is a difference between Organic and Non- Organic maple syrup. In order for us to label our maple syrup as “Certified Organic” we had to first apply and go through a thorough inspection of all our sugarbushes, sap gathering points, neighboring lands, our sugarhouse and all equipment, our commercial kitchen areas, our handling and packaging practices, our bookkeeping methods, etc. This inspection had to be done before we were approved by OEFFA to be certified organic. This also means that we will be inspected regularly and audited. Certifying our Farm organic means that we do not use any chemicals or pesticides nor do the neighboring lands. We do not use chemicals in maple syrup tapping, production or cleaning. We do not over tap our trees. We leave a very small footprint in the sugarbush. We work very hard at producing the finest quality organic maple syrup at our farm for your table and ours.

features: Wild Coffee: Our coffee bushes grow wild in the tropical rainforest of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in southern India. The forest is a sanctuary to several species of plants, animals, birds and more. Growing coffee in high-diversity shade is the most environmentally sustainable.

Organic and tasty, from the ground up: The abundant fertility of the forest enables the coffee to thrive without the need for any artificial chemical input. In fact, coffee grows wild, without having to be tended to. The coffees acquire some of the taste and aroma of the nearby plants in the forest (especially fruits and spices). The result is a character in the cup that is unique to the region.
Inhabited by the indigenous people of the Kurumba tribe, the livelihood from coffee helps them preserve their traditional ways of living, and in turn helps conserve their delicate natural habitats.

The berries are handpicked without the use of machinery so that only the fully ripe beans are harvested. Under ripe beans are left on the plants to ripen further. This selective picking ensures that the beans are at the peak of flavor when picked. They are then manually washed, pulped, and sun dried. Though this process takes much longer than mechanical drying, the slower drying period enhances the flavor in the beans.
The beans are then micro-roasted in small batches to bring out their full flavor and aroma.

description: This product made from miso and yuzu a Japanese citrus. You can use for not only salad, but also good for other dishes. Miso's origins can be traced to China as far back as the 4th century BC. The written word miso first appeared around 800 BC. In Japan, it is said that miso was introduced in the 7th century by Buddhist monks. The process of making miso was gradually refined and it became a vital part of the samurai diet. It was in the 17th century that industrial production of miso first began. High in protein and rich in vitamins and minerals, miso played an important nutritional role in feudal Japan. Miso is still widely used in Japan, both in traditional and modern cooking, but it has been gaining worldwide interest, as well. Marukome Co. Manufactures approximately 100, 000 tons of miso annually, making it Japan's largest producer. It means Marukome is the number 1 miso company in the world. This yuzu dressing is using yuzu juice and miso. Miso contains vitamins, magnesium, protein, sodium, carbohydrate, iron, and minerals. Made from fermented soybeans, rice, and koi miso is a thick paste-like substance. Also miso paste as known as "soy Bean Paste". It is brown in color and tastes pleasantly salty, tangy, and savory on its own. Also you can feel umami in miso taste. Miso has a surprisingly low Salt contents. While the most common use of miso is in Japanese-style miso soup. Japanese usually make miso soup with wake kelp, tofu, and green onion. You can make your original miso soup easily using miso and easy and your favorite toppings like cheese, tomato, corn, Popcorn, or batter. Also this product can use for salad, pickles, pasta, and carpaccio.

*I am a happy mad scientist with coffee.* That’s how I’ve been described, anyway. I love playing “what if”- blending Fair Trade Organic beans, roast profiles, and natural funky flavors. When I discover a blend that is, as my Dad would say, "as close to perfect as damn is to swearing," I package it up and pass it on to all my Coffee Junkie friends. Once you taste truly fresh-roasted, naturally flavored coffees...you'll become a Coffee Junkie for life, and I'm OK with that!   Why it's important to grind just what you need just before you brew? Coffee stays fresh in the bean form for 3+ months. If you grind your coffee it is best brewed within 1 month. So, if you are a real coffee junkie and want the freshest coffee on the planet then you will want to grind and brew, grind and brew and so on and so on... Brew coffee like a real Coffee Junkie at home Invest in a coffee grinder. Grind your coffee according to your brewing method. Basic rule of thumb is if you use a filter the grind is not as crucial as if you brew without a filter.   Grind 3 tblsp of coffee beans for an 8oz cup of coffee. If you prefer a bolder cup add a bit more coffee. Prefer cold brew? It's a piece of cake to make! Course grind 8oz of Coffee Junkie coffee and place grounds in a coffee filter tied with a twist tie and in a pitcher. Pour 1 gallon of filtered water in the pitcher. Refrigerate over night or up to 24 hours. Remove the coffee ground pouch and voila... cold brew that is as close to perfect as damn is to swearing!   If you have any questions please feel free to ask, your coffee/tea must be "as close to perfect as damn is to swearing" or my work is not complete!

description: Founded in 1972, Stash Tea Company originally operated out of an old Portland Victorian style house, supplying loose herbal teas and bulk herbs to natural food stores. Starting in 1975, the company broadened its focus to include bagged teas and then began to sell a full line of traditional, specialty blend and herbal teas directly to fine restaurants and through a mail order catalog to consumers. Today, Stash Tea Company is one of the largest specialty tea companies in the United States. The company derives its name from an entertaining aspect of tea folklore. In earlier centuries, tea was a valuable commodity traditionally transported by clipper ship. The ship’s captain often was presented with some of the finest teas for his personal use. This supply was his “stash,” stowed carefully as his “private reserve.” Today, the term is still used to denote anything put away carefully because of its preciousness.

features: Made with Green Bee Propolis from Brazilian Nature
description: Brazilian propolis is quite different from others produced all over the world. There are two main reasons for this. The first one is the type of bees. In Brazil we work with the Africanized Honey Bee (apis melifera scutelata). This special kind of bees has a different way to collect propolis in the plants. If there are 2 types of bees in an area, Africanized Honey Bees and European Honey Bees, they will produce different kinds of propolis. The second reason is the bio diversity of Brazilian flora. In North Hemisphere propolis is produced mainly by 2 types of plants. In Brazil, Propolis is found in more than 300 different types of plants. Researches made in Brazil and mainly in Japan show that the Green Type Propolis produced in some areas of Sao Paulo and Minas Gerais States in Brazil has the most contents of phenolic compounds, specially the flavonoids, and some esters very important. Uniflora is equipped with its own laboratory which permits total quality control of the various types of Propolis, permitting Uniflora to offer a products with various levels of concentration. Uniflora produces Propolis Extract in the concentrations 30% (Light), 45% (Medium), and 55% (Strong), as well as 60% Brix Alcohol Free. For the daily use. It is produced with 30% of propolis. We recommend it for external use, daily use. It is produced at 60 Brix Grade. This product is also Wax Free, which means, no wax when mix with water.

description: Product Description

Orville Redenbacher's Gourmet Popping Corn is the perfect snack to share with the family, and it's available in Movie Theater Butter, Butter, Butter Light, Smart Pop! 94% Fat Free, Kettle Korn, and many other great flavors.
About the Brand
Orville Redenbacher's namesake product comes in a variety of styles, including microwave, old-fashioned kernal, and pre-popped snacks

Orville Redenbacher, born in 1907 on a small farm in Indiana, got an early start in the popcorn business. As a kid, he earned his spending money popping and selling popcorn he grew on the family farm. Orville spent more than 60 years developing a corn hybrid unlike any other. He created and tested more than 40,000 varieties, until he found the one that popped up light, fluffy, and tasty enough to meet his standards. They are the same standards that have made Orville Redenbacher's Gourmet Popping Corn the favorite of so many families today.

In 1970, Orville started his popcorn company, naming it the Redbow Popcorn Company, and a year later, Orville Redenbacher's Gourmet Popping Corn was born. In 1976, Orville sold his company to Hunt-Wesson, but continued to act as the company's spokesperson in TV ads. Hunt-Wesson launched Orville Redenbacher's shelf-stable microwave popcorn in 1983. ConAgra Foods bought Hunt-Wesson and acquired the Orville Redenbacher's brand in 1990.
Orville passed away in 1995, but his namesake brand remains number one brand in the U.S.
Orville Redenbacher's Standards

"We grow and harvest our own corn with the highest quality standards. We also use special corn-harvesting machines, which reduces potential bruising to the kernels. After harvesting Orville's unique hybrid, the corn is slowly conditioned by drying it just enough so that each kernel reaches the optimum moisture level. Following the drying process, the kernels are carefully sifted three times and those that are too small or too light are rejected. Only acceptable kernels go onto the polisher and then the popcorn is sealed in jars or microwave packages for freshness."
About ConAgra

ConAgra Foods is one of the largest packaged foods companies in North America with major presence in retail outlets, foodservice and restaurants, and in ingredients. Their more than 70 brands--which include favorites such as Pam, Hunt's, Healthy Choice, Butterball, Wesson, Swiss Miss, Rotel, Peter Pan, Marie Callender's, Hebrew National, Wolf Brand Chili, Rosarita, Egg Beaters, Chef Boyardee, and more--are in 96% of U.S. households, and more than 30% of ConAgra Foods brands are number one in their category.

Rooibos grows exclusively in the Cederberg Mountain region and around Clanwilliam and Citrusdal. During summer and early autumn the plant’s branches are hand-harvested and cut into smaller pieces. The raw Rooibos is then moistened with water, thoroughly bruised then placed in heaps and allowed to oxidize for 8 to 24 hours. After oxidation, the herb is spread out in a special yard to dry naturally in the sun. We source our Rooibos directly from one of the pioneers of organic Rooibos processing in South Africa. description: There is no one recipe for mole. Throughout Mexico you’ll find many types of mole such as mole poblano, which has over 20 ingredients in it. Oaxaca, the land of seven moles, has (obviously) seven different popular mole recipes such as mole negro and mole verde. Pipian, mole amarillito, and mole coloradito are just a few others you will find throughout Mexico and Central America. Nearly all of them use chocolate, chiles, salt, cloves, pepper, and cinnamon.

Mole sauces are, naturally, the classic use for this particular blend. However, adding a pinch of it to baked beans, mixing it with butter and drowning a roasted cob of corn in it, adding it to brownies, or using it as a straight up rub are other great solutions. In addition, you can add a tablespoon of it to a bottle of vodka. Store in a dark place for a week. Filter through cheesecloth and use as a snazzy homemade booze for savory cocktails.
